deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 35-37): Grothendieck is encoding the combinatorial map C cut out of the real projective plane by an arrangement of three pseudo-lines (D_i), i in I, |I| = 3. The map has 3 vertices, 6 edges and 4 triangular faces; it is the hemi-octahedron, whose double cover is the octahedron, his 'octaèdre (gauche)'. On this page he describes everything in terms of the 1-skeleton K of the map, viewed as a 1-dimensional combinatorial complex together with its three sub-1-complexes D_i.

Step by step:
(1) K is the union of the distinct sub-complexes D_i. Each D_i is a bigon: a circle with a 2-element vertex set S_i and a 2-element edge set A_i.
(2) The vertex set of K is in canonical bijection with I: the vertex indexed by i is the unique vertex not on D_i, namely D_j ∩ D_k. Hence S_i ≅ I − {i}.
(3) Two-element sets are treated as Z/2-torsors, and ∧ denotes the contracted product of torsors. The orientations of the bigon D_i (i.e. of the pseudo-line) form the torsor Ω_i = S_i ∧ A_i. A pair (vertex s, edge a) means 'leave s along a', and changing either s or a reverses the orientation, so this is correct.
(4) He defines a twisted torsor 𝔏_i = Ω_i ∧ ∧_{α≠i}(I∖{α}). Since S_i = I∖{i} and T∧T is trivial, this is ≅ A_i ∧ ∧_{α∈I}(I∖{α}).
(5) He obtains the canonical isomorphisms (15):
   ∧_i Ω_i ≅ ∧_i 𝔏_i ≅ (∧_i A_i) ∧ ∧_{α∈I}(I∖{α}).
   - The first holds because each factor I∖{α} occurs twice over i ≠ α and cancels.
   - In the second, ∧_α(I∖{α}) ≅ or(I), the orientation torsor of the 3-element set I. A total order orders each 2-subset, and a permutation changes the result by its number of inversions, i.e. by its sign.
(6) The next page turns this into (15 bis): (∧Ω_i) ∧ or(I) ≅ ∧A_i. The left side is the orientation torsor of the octahedron defined by the family (Ω_i). The fact that K comes from the map C trivializes ∧A_i. This yields an equivalence between octahedra and 'skew octahedral graphs' equipped with a trivialization of ∧A_i.

Purpose: a purely combinatorial, torsor-theoretic description of how the orientation of the octahedral double cover is determined by the orientations of the three pseudo-lines. This is the local building block for a 'combinatorial maps / pseudo-line arrangements' theory, essentially the rank-3 sign (chirotope) calculus of oriented matroids, done in Grothendieck's torsor language.
errors: No mathematical errors found. All torsor identities check: S_i=I∖{i}; 𝔏_i ≅ A_i∧∧_{α∈I}(I∖α); ∧Ω_i≅∧𝔏_i; ∧_α(I∖α)≅or(I).
Minor imprecision: 'l'un des sommets de K ... est en corr. biun. avec I' should read 'l'ensemble des sommets de K'.

ideas.what: Orientation torsor of a bigon (combinatorial circle) as the contracted product S∧A of its vertex torsor and edge torsor
ideas.modern_name: Orientation double cover / determinant-type Z/2-torsor of a cell complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (combinatorial topology); torsor formalism in Grothendieck's school
ideas.where_published: Contracted products of torsors are standard in SGA/Giraud; this specific use is not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Canonical iso ∧_{α∈I}(I∖{α}) ≅ or(I) for a 3-element set
ideas.modern_name: Sign/orientation torsor of a finite set via pairwise orderings (inversion parity)

ideas.what: Encoding the arrangement of 3 pseudo-lines in RP^2 (hemi-octahedron) and the orientation of its octahedral double cover via Z/2-torsors built from the pseudo-line orientations
ideas.modern_name: Rank-3 oriented matroids / chirotope sign conventions; topological representation of pseudo-line arrangements

missed.claim: Grothendieck develops, in torsor/categorical language, the sign bookkeeping relating orientations of pseudo-lines to orientations of the octahedral double cover. This is essentially the local (3-element) chirotope calculus of rank-3 oriented matroids, done independently of and without reference to that literature. It is a categorical reformulation rather than a new result.
missed.quote: Ω_i = S_i ∧ A_i ... l'une des orientations du bigone D_i, i.e. de la ps. droite D_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild historical interest: it shows Grothendieck's c.1981 pseudo-line work parallels the oriented matroid theory then emerging. It gives a functorial, torsor-based (choice-free) formulation of orientation data that could be of minor expository value.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but routine torsor bookkeeping, a step in an unpublished development of pseudo-line arrangements and combinatorial maps. Historically interesting as evidence of Grothendieck independently working in oriented-matroid territory, but nothing on this page would surprise a specialist mathematically.
